paragraphs.source_en: Small-sized images are also numerous, present either on the same walls as large compositions or located on separate walls. Being only several centimetres high they were easy to execute by a single individual. Since they are often present on lateral walls away from the large compositions, these small figures might indicate a private painting activity, important for an individual or a group but not significant for a large community.

paragraphs.source_en: Is there any difference in the themes and painted elements between the large compositions and small figures? The characteristic elements of the Round Head complex are present in both large and small paintings with the only exception being the Great Gods, which are always of large dimensions. All elements being present in the whole complex indicate that they were important for both public and private image-making, and the same painted elements suggest that the identity of a group and of an individual were the same.

paragraphs.source_en: If the sites were chosen as places for rituals or ceremonies they were likely to have been considered sacred. Large paintings in such sites would represent what can be called official art designated for the public. Small figures present in the same sites might represent paintings made by individuals in these sacred places, perhaps requests for personal wishes or private religious expression. In other words, sacred places used for public rituals or ceremonies would also be the attraction for single painters wishing to leave their message on the rock wall. Painted sites were thus an object of both public and private religious expression.
